title: Platelet-derived Growth Factor Receptor-alpha Induces Contraction Knots and Inflammatory Pain-like Behavior in a Rat Model of Myofascial Trigger Points.
authors: Liu, Yu; Jin, Feihong; Zhou, Lingwei; Li, Xuan; Li, Xiaoyue; Chen, Qinghe; Yang, Shaozhong; Sun, Jintang; Qi, Feng
one_liner_zh: 该文研究肌筋膜触发点中PDGFR-alpha信号通路与疼痛行为，未涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Myofascial trigger points (MTrPs) are the primary etiological characteristics of chronic myofascial pain syndrome. Receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs) are associated with signal transduction in the central mechanisms of chronic pain, but the role of RTKs in the peripheral mechanisms of MTrPs remains unclear. The current study aimed to identify RTKs expression in MTrPs and elucidate the molecular mechanisms through which platelet-derived growth factor receptor-alpha (PDGFR-alpha) induces contraction knots and inflammatory pain-like behavior in a rat model of myofascial trigger points. METHODS: MTrPs tissue samples were obtained from the trapezius muscles of patients with myofascial pain syndrome through needle biopsy, and PDGFR-alpha activation was analyzed by microarray, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and histological staining. Sprague-Dawley rats (male and female) were used to investigate PDGFR-alpha signaling, assessing pain-like behaviors with Randall-Selitto and nest-building tests. Muscle fiber and sarcomere morphologies were observed using histology and electron microscopy. The PDGFR-alpha binding protein was identified by coimmunoprecipitation, liquid chromatograph mass spectrometer, and molecular docking. PDGFR-alpha-related protein or gene levels, muscle contraction, and inflammatory markers were determined by Western blot and reverse-transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction. RESULTS: PDGFR-alpha phosphorylation levels were elevated in the MTrPs tissues of individuals with trapezius muscle pain and were positively correlated with pain intensity. In rats, PDGFR-alpha activation caused pain-like behaviors and muscle contraction via the Janus kinase 2/signal transducer and activator of transcription-3 (JAK2/STAT3) pathway. JAK2/STAT3 inhibitors reversed the pain-like behaviors and muscle contraction induced by PDGFR-alpha activation. Collagen type I alpha 1 (COL1A1) binds to PDGFR-alpha and promotes its phosphorylation, which contributed to pain-like behaviors and muscle contraction. CONCLUSIONS: COL1A1-induced phosphorylation of PDGFR-alpha and the subsequent activation of the JAK2/STAT3 pathway may induce dysfunctional muscle contraction and increased nociception at MTrPs.
abstract_zh: 背景：肌筋膜触发点（MTrPs）是慢性肌筋膜疼痛综合征的主要病因学特征。受体酪氨酸激酶（RTKs）与慢性疼痛中枢机制中的信号转导相关，但RTKs在MTrPs外周机制中的作用仍不清楚。本研究旨在识别MTrPs中的RTKs表达，并阐明血小板衍生生长因子受体-α（PDGFR-alpha）在肌筋膜触发点大鼠模型中诱导收缩结节和炎症性疼痛样行为的分子机制。方法：通过针刺活检获取肌筋膜疼痛综合征患者斜方肌的MTrPs组织样本，并通过微阵列、酶联免疫吸附试验和组织学染色分析PDGFR-alpha的激活。使用Sprague-Dawley大鼠（雄性和雌性）研究PDGFR-alpha信号传导，通过Randall-Selitto和筑巢测试评估疼痛样行为。使用组织学和电子显微镜观察肌纤维和肌节形态。通过免疫共沉淀、液相色谱质谱联用和分子对接鉴定PDGFR-alpha结合蛋白。通过Western blot和逆转录定量聚合酶链反应测定PDGFR-alpha相关蛋白或基因水平、肌肉收缩和炎症标志物。结果：在斜方肌疼痛个体的MTrPs组织中，PDGFR-alpha磷酸化水平升高，并与疼痛强度呈正相关。在大鼠中，PDGFR-alpha激活通过Janus激酶2/信号转导和转录激活因子-3（JAK2/STAT3）通路引起疼痛样行为和肌肉收缩。JAK2/STAT3抑制剂逆转了PDGFR-alpha激活诱导的疼痛样行为和肌肉收缩。I型胶原蛋白α1（COL1A1）与PDGFR-alpha结合并促进其磷酸化，这有助于疼痛样行为和肌肉收缩。结论：COL1A1诱导的PDGFR-alpha磷酸化及随后的JAK2/STAT3通路激活可能诱导MTrPs处的功能障碍性肌肉收缩和伤害感受增强。
